blogs.title: The Geometry of Creativity: Why Neuron Angles Matter in AI Art
blogs.description: Take a deep dive into the core theory behind this paper. We'll explain why the standard 'Euclidean' way of thinking about neural network weights is flawed for preserving creativity, and how the concept of 'Hyperspherical Energy' on a sphere reveals that the *angles* between neurons are the true carriers of semantic meaning. Learn how shifting these angles allows us to instruct an AI without breaking its ability to generate photorealistic images.

blogs.title: DreamBooth on Steroids: Generating Your Dog in a Spacesuit in Seconds
blogs.description: Subject-driven generation (like DreamBooth) often struggles with model collapse or losing context when trained for too long. Discover how Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) solves this stability crisis. This post breaks down how OFT allows you to teach a model new concepts with fewer images and training epochs, ensuring your generated subject remains consistent even after hundreds of iterations.

blogs.title: ControlNet's Lightweight Cousin: Ultimate Grayscale Control Without Inference Overhead
blogs.description: ControlNet is powerful but heavy; LoRA is light but sometimes lacks precision. Explore how OFT offers the best of both worlds: it introduces extreme control signals (like edges or segmentation maps) with minimal trainable parameters and zero additional runtime cost. See how this method achieves sharper adherence to control signals than current state-of-the-art methods, making it accessible for real-time applications.

blogs.title: From Purple Goo to Perfect Poses: Solving Convergence Instability in Diffusion Models
blogs.description: Training diffusion models can be treacherous, requiring hyperparameters that are sensitive to the slightest change. This blog post demystifies 'Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning' (COFT), a variant introduced in the paper that acts as a safety net during training. We'll show empirical evidence of how this constraint leads to smooth, predictable convergence, saving researchers from getting stuck in local optima or generating hallucinated artifacts.
